name: Temple AI Campus
subtitle: 100 MW IT • four 25 MW phases • Central Texas
verdict: Diligence only: approval hold and base returns below hurdle
thesis: A water-conserving, liquid-cooled capacity campus in North Temple can be a credible development option only if land, a 140 MW power pathway, regulatory clearance and bankable tenant demand are proven.
executiveSummary: Develop and lease powered/cooled capacity in four 25 MW IT phases. The base asset includes buildings, power distribution, emergency standby systems and cooling; customers supply compute and networking hardware.

Select the historically advertised 147-acre Moores Mill/Wendland industrial area for investigation. Its address and utility context are source-backed; current land availability, boundaries and 140 MW service capacity remain unverified.

Texas is currently a gated development opportunity: TCEQ explicitly includes data-center construction stormwater applications in the statewide hold. A new project has no demonstrated Batch Zero eligibility. Model operation at months 48/54/60/66 only after a future authorized start.

Use dry heat rejection with mechanical trim and 140 MW peak electrical demand. Base underwriting yields approximately 10.2% equity IRR against a 14% hurdle; improve evidenced rent/cost terms before FID. No tax incentive, energy-trading profit or on-site gas shortcut is assumed.

site.name: Moores Mill / Wendland study area
site.addressOrArea: Southwest corner of Moores Mill Road and Wendland Road, North Temple, Texas; historical 147-acre EDC announcement
site.coordinateBasis: OSM road reference on Moores Mill Road, not a tract centroid, exact intersection or boundary. Official EDC source supplies the candidate area address; a title/survey gate must locate the actual parcel.
site.landStatus: Historical 2020 EDC site announcement only. Current owner, availability, land control, parcel ID and usable area are NOT verified.
site.rationale: Investigate a documented industrial area with road and municipal utility context on the Central Texas corridor. Selection is provisional and can be displaced by a competing site with a proven earlier power date.
constraints: No title, option, survey, environmental assessment or current availability evidence.
Industrial promotion does not establish data-center zoning or a feasible campus fit.
Floodplain, drainage, wetlands, geotechnical conditions, airport/FAA height constraints, easements and neighboring receptors need parcel-level screening.
Two carrier-diverse entrances and route diversity must be demonstrated; area internet service proves neither.
Utility nomination is provisional: Oncor serves much of the area, but parcel-specific DSP/TSP must confirm jurisdiction.

alternatives.name: Five Points Business Park, Abilene
alternatives.reason: DCOA identifies over 500 acres of industrial sites and an on-site 50 MW substation. Its stated capacity is below the 140 MW campus peak and says nothing about spare headroom.
alternatives.decision: Reserve candidate; proceed only if a TSP study and actual lot assembly show an earlier viable connection. The same state approval hold applies.

alternatives.name: Texas Central Park, Waco
alternatives.reason: The City identifies a large established industrial park at I-35/SH6/US84 with advertised development land. No site-specific 140 MW connection evidence found.
alternatives.decision: Reserve candidate with a parallel owner/utility desktop screen. Temple wins only provisionally on a documented 147-acre investigation area, not a proven power advantage.

power.strategy: Grid-supplied campus with non-exporting emergency standby and UPS; reserve and disclose the full 140 MW peak campus requirement at the outset.
power.gridRoute: Confirm DSP/TSP, service territory and viable POI; seek post-hold intake direction; execute intermediate agreement and studies, post required security, prove load dynamics and ride-through, conclude SLLIA and utility works, then obtain explicit staged energization permission. 138 kV is a design placeholder, not an offered voltage.
power.generationRoute: Emergency generators only in base CAPEX; no prime-power gas plant. A gas alternative would need fuel pressure/capacity, air permit, acoustic study, heat rejection and a separate finance case. Off-grid or behind-the-meter generation is not presumed exempt from the data-center permit hold.
power.utility: Oncor is the provisional area utility; exact interconnecting DSP/TSP unconfirmed. Retail supply requires a separate qualified supplier agreement.
constraints: No capacity allocated, interconnection application filed, SLLIA signed or energization date offered.
75 MW large-load threshold uses aggregate site demand; dividing the campus into 25 MW phases does not avoid review.
Batch Zero July 2026 filing dates have passed. No historic eligibility is claimed.
140 MW study request implies USD7m intermediate security plus USD0.1m study fee under adopted rule; later security may be higher.
Power-quality and dynamic models must capture UPS, chiller motor starts, IT step loads, curtailment, restoration and fault ride-through.
Do not monetize emergency generators as routine dispatch or assume their air permits allow economic load-following.

cooling.strategy: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling with isolated facility/CDU loops, dry coolers and air-cooled mechanical trim sized for peak conditions. Separate residual room-air cooling; N+1 modular equipment and sectional isolation target maintainability.
cooling.climateImplications: Central Texas heat means free cooling cannot carry the year. Annual PUE target 1.28, peak facility design PUE 1.40; verify 43 C design and 46 C stress condition against vendor curves, local hourly data, cold snaps and hail/wind loads.
cooling.waterStrategy: Avoid evaporative towers in the base design. Assume 15 m3/day domestic/service demand plus initial closed-loop fill and fire reserve; closed-loop circulation is not consumptive water withdrawal. Meter mains, makeup and discharge separately, obtain City capacity and drought conditions, and plan TWDB reporting. No water rights or well permit assumed.

commercial.customer: One creditworthy hyperscaler or AI-infrastructure operator as 50 MW anchor, plus a second 25-50 MW customer if commercially justified; no customer has been contacted or secured.
commercial.offering: 15-year wholesale committed-capacity leases, four 25 MW IT modules, customer-owned servers/network, documented liquid-interface and density envelope, separate metered electricity pass-through.
commercial.contracting: Secure binding take-or-pay capacity and ramp milestones with parent guarantee or bank security before FID. Specify rent start only after acceptance, utility-availability conditions, cancellation/extension rights, power-price allocation, liquid temperatures, permissible curtailment, SLA exclusions/remedies and change-order boundaries. Initial term is 15 years per accepted phase. Model revenue thereafter is an explicit uncontracted renewal assumption; do not describe it as take-or-pay coverage.
commercial.financing: Illustrative 60% debt, 8% rate, 15-year amortization; 14% nominal equity hurdle. Use construction-to-term debt only after legal restart, power agreement, permits, guaranteed maximum price scope and creditworthy prelease. Hold USD7m utility security separately; final requirement may be larger. No incentive or refinance proceeds assumed.
goToMarket: Create a confidential tenant brief with independently verified power pathway, parcel and heat-removal envelope.
Screen anchor credit and workload: training/inference mix, uninterrupted service expectation, liquid supply temperature, rack density, curtailment tolerance and ramp certainty.
Obtain competing capacity-rent proposals using identical electricity pass-through and fit-out boundary.
Execute milestone-linked 50 MW anchor lease and option remaining phases; build later blocks only against contracted demand.
counterpartyQuestions: Will a tenant guarantee 50 MW at a specified rent and cooling interface before lender commitments?
Can the utility offer 140 MW peak campus service with a binding cost/ramp and acceptable curtailment terms?
Will the landowner grant a diligence option conditioned on planning, power and financing?
Will two carriers certify separate physical paths and entry points, rather than reselling the same route?
What deposits, cancellation exposure and thermal derates will OEMs actually contract?

assumptions.label: Campus IT capacity
assumptions.basis: Four independent 25 MW phases; owner design brief, excludes GPU procurement.

assumptions.label: Gross study envelope
assumptions.basis: 147 historic acres converts to 59.49 ha; use 59.5 ha only as an area envelope, not surveyed usable area.

assumptions.label: Annual PUE
assumptions.basis: Planning target for warm-climate, direct-liquid cooling with air-cooled heat rejection and mechanical trim; hourly weather simulation pending.

assumptions.label: Peak design PUE
assumptions.basis: Peak facility capacity 140 MW at 100 MW IT; deliberately distinct from annual PUE. Hot-weather equipment derating and auxiliary motor starts still need studies.

assumptions.label: Delivered electricity
assumptions.basis: All-in planning allowance: energy 45 + delivery/demand equivalent 20 + supply shaping, losses, fees and tax allowance 15. This is not a current tariff or supplier quote. Test 55-125.

assumptions.label: Facility construction
assumptions.basis: Order-of-magnitude allowance: shell 1800 + electrical/UPS/standby 4000 + cooling 2200 + civil/drainage 1000 + controls/security/fiber 500 + testing/commissioning 500. Excludes separate land and off-plot utility connection; includes customer-owned HV substation; includes procurement taxes without assumed exemption. Test +/-30%.

assumptions.label: Land acquisition allowance
assumptions.basis: 147 acres at approximately USD81,600/acre as an underwriting placeholder, not an owner ask or appraisal.

assumptions.label: HV connection and upgrades
assumptions.basis: Off-plot utility connection and system-upgrade allowance. Customer-owned HV substation and downstream campus electrical are inside facility hard costs. The study result may materially exceed it.

assumptions.label: Primary generation
assumptions.basis: No primary gas plant in base case. Emergency standby plant included in facility electrical budget.

assumptions.label: Soft costs
assumptions.basis: Owner development, engineering, permitting, legal and delivery management allowance applied by model; does not include GPU/cloud costs.

assumptions.label: Construction contingency
assumptions.basis: Concept allowance on model-defined construction cost base; uncertainty is broader than this reserve.

assumptions.label: Fixed operating costs
assumptions.basis: Stabilized allowance: property tax 18 + insurance 4 + staff/security 6 + administration/compliance 2. No property-tax incentive assumed; appraisal and tax districts unconfirmed.

assumptions.label: Variable facility operating cost
assumptions.basis: Occupied-capacity allowance for variable consumables and maintenance; fixed OPEX covers baseline maintenance exposure on unleased commissioned space; electricity pass-through excluded.

assumptions.label: Capacity lease
assumptions.basis: Illustrative 15-year committed-capacity base rent, electricity passed through separately; no customer quote or signed lease. Test 150-250. Beyond each initial 15-year lease, the 20-year project model assumes uninterrupted reletting at unchanged rent and occupancy, no downtime or renewal CAPEX. This is an uncontracted tail of 60/54/48/42 months by phase, not secured revenue.

assumptions.label: Stabilized committed occupancy
assumptions.basis: 90 MW leased when fully built; owner exposure remains on unleased capacity. No prelease exists.

assumptions.label: Metered IT load factor
assumptions.basis: Average draw as share of committed IT capacity; independent from occupancy.

assumptions.label: Construction/term debt
assumptions.basis: Illustrative leverage, 8% annual rate and 15-year amortization; subject to tenant credit, debt sizing and legal reopen.

assumptions.label: Equity discount rate
assumptions.basis: Sponsor screening hurdle; no investor commitment.

assumptions.label: First phase operation
assumptions.basis: Conditional M48 COD: M12 HV order, 30-month manufacture/delivery to M42, installation/SAT M42-46, integrated acceptance M46-48. Clock starts only after regulatory release; all milestones require written supplier/utility evidence.

assumptions.label: Phase interval
assumptions.basis: 25 MW at model months 48/54/60/66 if capacity, demand and delivery gates pass.

assumptions.label: Interconnection intermediate security floor
assumptions.basis: 140 MW requested peak x USD50,000/MW. Final security may exceed this; excludes USD0.1m study fee budgeted in soft costs. Return/credit/forfeiture depends on rule and agreement.

assumptions.label: Operations domestic water planning demand
assumptions.basis: Sanitary, cleaning and limited makeup assumption, plus separately designed fire storage and initial closed-loop fill. No evaporative cooling in base case and no municipal capacity commitment.

assumptions.label: Heat-rejection design ambient
assumptions.basis: Preliminary hot-weather screening condition, stress test 46 C; not a certified ASHRAE local design percentile.

assumptions.label: Liquid capture and water temperatures
assumptions.basis: Shared engineering worksheet assumes 90% liquid capture at 35/45 C supply/return, with 10% room cooling; customer requirements can force colder water and greater trim-chiller demand.

assumptions.label: Post-lease renewal revenue
assumptions.unit: months beyond 15-year initial leases by phase
assumptions.basis: Project horizon is 20 years from first operation. Model assumes uninterrupted renewals/reletting at unchanged occupancy/rent after initial leases, with zero downtime or renewal investment; no contracts exist. Lender case must haircut/remove the tail.

killCriteria: No lawful route to advance or no credible post-hold intake after a sponsor-defined six-month review: stop discretionary development spend and retain only low-cost options.
Landowner cannot establish an available contiguous parcel and at least the engineered usable footprint free of fatal easements/flood constraints: replace site.
Utility cannot establish an economically viable 140 MW peak pathway, or upgrade scope exceeds the underwriting case without tenant compensation: do not FID.
No creditworthy 50 MW anchor prelease, downside DSCR below 1.30, or stressed equity return below sponsor hurdle: resize capital commitment or stop.
Municipal water/fire service, non-evaporative thermal performance, air/noise compliance or genuinely diverse fiber cannot be proven: do not promise capacity.
nextActions: Week 1: obtain regulatory counsel interpretation of the current state hold and permissible diligence; do not file or start works based on assumed exemptions.
Week 1: request EDC/current owner parcel IDs, updated availability, asking terms, survey, easements and option conditions; no offer or outreach has been sent.
Week 1-2: establish parcel-specific DSP/TSP and request a full 140 MW intake/POI discussion, with a 25/50/75/100 MW IT ramp and dynamic-load brief.
Week 2: commission scoped desktop environmental/flood/airport screening and municipal water/fire-flow and zoning determinations.
Week 2-4: request indicative electrical/cooling/OEM packages, independent carrier routes and anchor-tenant requirements; replace model assumptions with dated responses.
At the first gate: approve only a capped diligence budget; release equipment deposits, construction and finance commitments against independently verified gates.
Use texas-execution.md for unsent utility/landowner/OEM requests, phase acceptance criteria, O&M staffing assumptions and anchor lease terms; no template has been dispatched.
